newsitem.title: UK: Metal prices retreat as copper rally attempt fails.
newsitem.headline: Metal prices retreat as copper rally attempt fails.

text.p: Prices retreated on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Wednesday after rally attempts earlier in the week failed to stimulate a surge in prices.
Speculative buying, much of it from North America, propped up the market as it fell towards the psychological $1,900 level, one floor trader said.
"I think it was the same speculators who were trying to push it through $1,970 yesterday," he said.
The three month market slipped to $1,907 in the afternoon, the weakest level since prices dipped to $1,895 on October 8.

However, more bullish traders argued prices should be helped by LME warehouse stocks being likely to continue to decline, putting pressure on readily available metal with scrap supplies remaining tight.
Aluminium came off its low when earlier speculative selling met solid support and the market finished at $1,342, down $14.
Among the precious metals, palladium continued to bump along at its lowest levels since September 1993.
Palladium has been fixed at $116.25 per ounce twice on Tuesday and already on Wednesday morning, the lowest number since it was at $115.75 over three years ago.
Dealers said palladium was caught between oversupply and low consumer demand and speculator interest was non existent.
Gold was also largely friendless and indicated at $381.75, just 40 cents up on the Tuesday closing level.
Activity in the soft commodity markets was mixed, although overall bearish sentiment prevailed, traders said.
An early rally in coffee prices based on a bigger than expected stock drawdown came apart when selling came out of New York and the London market followed.
"We are expecting heavy arrivals of coffee to be landed from Central America and that is keeping prices down," a trader said.
Cocoa was narrowly firmer after the origin countries relaxed their selling campaign of the past few days.
But traders said prices would remain under pressure as deliveries from the major producer Ivory Coast were expected in volume soon.
Sugar was weaker after being hit by speculator profit taking on Tuesday and the December futures contract was marked down 40 cents at $319.40 at 1607 GMT.
The oil market's flag ship Brent blend futures price edged back from post-Gulf War highs struck earlier in the week as traders took profits.
The most active December month was down 13 cents at $23.98 a barrel but traders noted the market was still underpinned by tight stocks in the United States and north west Europe.
UK grains futures were nervous and grain prices slithered in most of Europe this week as prices came under pressure from abundant supply.
